problem: Portrait treatment is mixed with passport, mugshot and school-photo output rules.
preserve: Facial value separation and restrained retouching.
proposedAction: Keep document-photo profiles separate from reusable portrait treatment.
validation: Apply the treatment to a pitcher; only the document profile may enforce its crop.

problem: Golden-hour and neon labels combine light, time and implied surroundings.
preserve: Direction, softness, falloff and color relationships.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: all 15 lights rewritten as modifiers that name source position, size, hardness, falloff and color and keep the prompt's subject and setting; 5 new lights (dappled leaf, horror underlight, theatrical follow spot, moonlight, lightning flash) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: A requested midday interior must not acquire a sunset landscape.

problem: Film-stock anchors and process artifacts are coupled to sample-camera presentation.
preserve: Grain scale, contrast curve and highlight behavior.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: all 13 stocks and processes rewritten as capture modifiers (emulsion color, grain, contrast curve, halation, lens) that keep the prompt's subject and setting and add no borders; inherited 'noisy'/'blurry' negatives removed where they suppressed grain; renamed SP01-018 Wet Plate Ambrotype, SP01-019 Black-and-White Infrared Film and SP01-026 Pinhole Long Exposure to stop overlapping Photography Eras; 7 new processes (redscale, Super 8, pushed Tri-X, cross-processed slide, bleach bypass, lith print, film soup) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Compare the same subject and framing under each emulsion-like response.

problem: GoPro and drone viewpoints share a category with events and documentary subjects.
preserve: Observational framing and camera-specific geometry.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 9 presets rewritten; GoPro, drone and new viewpoint presets are profiles that own only the camera, documentary treatments witness the prompt without adding events; 11 new presets (layered color, telephoto compression, hard shadow, reflections, slow shutter, over-under, typology, oblique aerial, frame-within-frame, humanist, high-ISO night) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Street treatment must not turn an object request into a street scene.

problem: Product, architecture, flat lay and food combine domains with incompatible framing rules.
preserve: Material clarity and controlled commercial lighting.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 14 presets rewritten so each keeps the supplied object and owns only its commercial mechanism; flat lay, packshot, e-commerce and ghost mannequin declare that they own the camera or backdrop; 6 new presets (dark chiaroscuro food, twilight exterior, hard-light glass, lifestyle in-hand, color-block set, ghost mannequin) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Preserve a supplied object; flat lay should change camera only when selected.

problem: Landscape, wildlife and macro can substitute expected subjects for the requested content.
preserve: Depth handling, fine-detail scale and tonal separation.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 6 presets rewritten as nature-photography approaches that keep the requested subject (an animal request stays an animal); astrophotography limited to telescope deep-sky; 14 new presets (bird in flight, camera trap, long-exposure seascape, Milky Way nightscape, supercell storm, intimate forest, backlit botanical, high-key snow, low-key rim-lit, focus-stacked specimen, nature abstract, wide-angle habitat, minimalist fog, blackwater dive) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: An animal request must not become a mountain merely because landscape tone was selected.

problem: Sensor simulation, camera installation and specialist output are grouped together.
preserve: Distinct sensor transfer curves and acquisition artifacts.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 12 presets rewritten; CCTV, dashcam, forensic, medical, Brenizer and tiny planet declare the viewpoint or framing they own, thermal and long exposure transfer as signal modifiers; SP01-028 renamed Ironbow Thermal Imaging (pack_02 has Thermal Camera); SP01-030 limited to false-color space-telescope mapping; 8 new lab and camera techniques (schlieren, photoelastic, slit-scan, chronophotography, tiny planet, UV fluorescence, Kirlian, borescope) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Thermal color may transfer; a CCTV overlay requires the capture profile.

problem: Genre names also carry wardrobe, sets and expected story situations.
preserve: Contrast design, shot rhythm and photographic finish.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 16 genres rewritten as cinema treatments (camera, light, stock, grade) that keep the prompt's setting and add no genre costumes or plot; franchise and real-name references removed from DNA; SP02-010 renamed 70s Kung Fu Studio Epic and SP02-012 Symmetrical Storybook Cinema because names enter the prompt; 4 new genres (German Expressionist, 80s sword-and-sorcery, Italian neorealism, peplum) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: An ordinary domestic activity must retain its setting under film-noir treatment.

problem: Broadcast layouts and TV looks can impose hosts, captions, weather or sports subjects.
preserve: Signal cadence, set-light grammar and broadcast framing.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 23 broadcast formats rewritten; treatments keep the prompt's content and never add a presenter, host or ticker, while graphic formats (bulletin crawl, forecast, radar, replay, security quad split, signal break) own the layout with textless shapes; the six near-duplicate pairs are separated by mechanism (set grammar vs tape signal, studio look vs chroma key, amateur studio vs bulletin slide, split-screen vs demo gloss, live feed vs telestrator replay, forecast map vs radar sweep); renamed Fisheye Glam Music Video, 90s Grunge Music Video and Marker-Edge Improvised Sitcom Cartoon to drop real names and brands.
validation: A video treatment must not add a presenter or fabricated ticker.

problem: Studio references combine recognizable character design with medium-specific rendering.
preserve: Line economy, cel boundaries, painted backgrounds and stop-motion cues.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 15 animation media rewritten so the subject is redrawn in the medium and no studio cast or mascot is added; nine studio or franchise names replaced by technique names (they reach the card-generation prompt); 5 new media (shadow-puppet silhouette, pinscreen, charcoal erasure, 70s limited TV, direct-on-film) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: A non-character subject must retain its identity without a studio-like cast.

problem: Historical process labels can add period clothing, aging props and card framing.
preserve: Emulsion response, tonal range and process-specific surfaces.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 12 historic processes rewritten as modifiers that keep a modern subject modern and own only the process, print surface and plate or print edges; overlaps with pack_01 film stocks separated (projected Kodachrome slide, physical Polaroid print, 90s lab print, Holga leaks, glass negative, color infrared, paper-negative pinhole); SP02-129 kept; 7 new processes (salt print, albumen carte de visite, pictorialist platinum, hand-colored lantern slide, mammoth plate, 1970s faded print, 1980s pocket Instamatic) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: A modern appliance remains modern under a historical photo process.

problem: Many light names overlap photo lighting while atmospheric wording adds environmental cues.
preserve: Cinematic contrast ratios and motivated light direction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 cinematic lights rewritten as film-set lighting modifiers (large sources, negative fill, haze, practicals, grade) that keep content and location constant; 12 names that duplicated pack_01 Lighting Techniques renamed to their cinema variant (Magic Hour Backlight, Blue Hour Cinematography, Cinematic Chiaroscuro Key, Neon Practical Noir, Hazed Window Shafts, Cinematic Silhouette Backdrop, Cinematic Split Key, Old Hollywood Beauty Key, Candlelit Low-Light Cinema, Bioluminescent Fantasy Glow, Club Strobe Stutter, Motion Light Trails) and SP02-080 to Anamorphic Overflare; old names kept as search aliases.
validation: Keep content constant and distinguish the light, not a changed location.

problem: The former cartoon DNA bundled drawing mechanics with named cast, setting and gag cues; the active fields have been separated from those cues.
preserve: Shape exaggeration, line character and comedic visual timing.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: authored DNA kept; 17 names that were show titles or a real person replaced by their drawing mechanism (old names kept as search aliases); 3 new briefs per preset with no repeated subject and only one slime monster (the preset that asks for it).
validation: A household object can use caricature without becoming a named character or topical scene.

problem: Three sensor looks overlap specialist imaging and CGI technical shaders.
preserve: X-ray, thermal and low-light signal differences.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: X-ray, thermal and night vision rewritten as sensor profiles that add no readouts or diagnoses (thermal is now white-hot greyscale, distinct from pack_01 ironbow); 17 new sensor outputs (ultrasound, MRI, CT volume, side-scan sonar, radar scope, multispectral and SAR satellite, starlight camera, scintigraphy, hyperspectral cube, seismic section, ground-penetrating radar, cloud and bubble chambers, retinal fundus, confocal fluorescence, night lights) bring the category to 20, pending cards; lab techniques stay in pack_01::7 and CGI passes go to pack_03::8.
validation: Verify no invented medical claim or diagnostic label is added to an image.

problem: Whiteboard, cave and skateboard imply different supports and output objects.
preserve: Tool marks, surface resistance and limited-color drawing.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 6 DIY media rewritten so the subject is drawn with the tool on the support and the support is never added as an object (the skateboard graphic no longer draws a board); brand and site references removed; 14 new supports and tools (notebook margin ballpoint, sticky-note mosaic, toy screen line, fogged mirror, beach sand, carved desk, kraft bag, graph-paper pixels, dusty car window, crayon rubbing, skin doodle, glowing peg board, gear-ring spirals, bedsheet banner) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: The subject stays intact; a drawing treatment must not add a skateboard.

problem: Renderer names are being used as style identity without isolating observable differences.
preserve: Sampling finish, specular handling, bounce-light and edge behavior.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 10 renderer presets rewritten by observable light transport, sampling and material behavior rather than brand (spectral dispersion and glare, real-time GI with TAA softness, biased motion-graphics GI, film VFX subsurface and volumes, principled denoised path tracing, archviz sun and sky, product HDRI swatches, feature-animation colored shadows, matcap sculpt, post-heavy game pipeline); SP03-008 renamed Feature Animation Path Tracer to drop the studio name; 10 new render behaviors (90s scanline, classic raytracer, radiosity, grey clay test, progressive noise, gaussian splats, baked lightmaps, lookdev plate, live-action integration, film-emulated CG) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Blind comparison should reveal different light/material behavior, not just branding.

problem: Glass, liquid and subsurface effects mix physical material changes with rendering behavior.
preserve: Refraction, scattering, roughness and specular response.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 13 CGI materials rewritten as modifiers that change only the target's material (shape, surroundings, light setup and camera kept); caustics made a light response of the named glass or water; 7 new material responses not already in pack_09 (thin-film iridescence, molten glowing metal, precious opal, gummy candy, pearlescent flake paint, aerogel, amber resin inclusion) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Only the requested target changes material; surroundings and camera remain unchanged.

problem: Atmospheric and environment-map terms may add fog or a new environment unintentionally.
preserve: Global illumination, shadow softness and light-volume behavior.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 8 CGI lights rewritten as rendered lighting setups that keep geometry, setting and camera (neutral product geometry unchanged); fog and shaft presets add only the medium their own lights need; SP03-038 renamed Rendered Rim Light Rig and SP03-041 Rendered Volumetric Shafts to stop duplicating pack_01 and pack_02 names; 12 new CGI lights (emissive-only, IES wall wash, physical sky, volumetric cloud linings, gobo patterns, RGB colored shadows, two-tone ramp, overcast dome, hard noon sun, stadium multi-shadow, aurora, eclipse) bring the category to 20, pending cards.
validation: Neutral product geometry remains unchanged when lighting is replaced.

problem: Clay, voxel and low-poly media sit beside isometric camera and cutaway profiles.
preserve: Mesh simplification and stylized surface construction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 stylized 3D presets rewritten; media (clay, low poly, voxel, metaballs, NURBS, fractal, glitch, toon, papercraft, toy bricks, origami) keep the requested view, while isometric, knolling, app icon and clay UI declare the view or layout they own; SP03-070 now means the 90s pre-rendered CD-ROM scene to stay distinct from the new 90s renderer presets; SP03-077 renamed Toy Brick-Built 3D to drop the brand; 3D typography uses invented glyphs.
validation: Switch media without changing requested view; selecting isometric is an explicit exception.

problem: Game assets, product shots and architecture impose different delivery formats.
preserve: Edge treatment, contact shadows and manufactured construction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 11 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 9 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_03__hard-surface-and-product-cgi.md.
validation: A hero product image must not become a multi-view asset sheet without a request.

problem: T-pose, medical illustration, food and collectible-avatar formats constrain subject identity.
preserve: Organic shading, soft volumes and anatomical readability.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 7 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 13 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_03__organic-character-and-bio-cgi.md.
validation: Do not force a person into a T-pose or transform a requested object into an avatar.

problem: City, forest, VR and scientific entries prescribe worlds rather than only render appearance.
preserve: Depth organization and environment-specific material logic.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 9 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 11 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_03__environment-and-worldbuilding.md.
validation: A retained environment direction is labeled as such; portable variants preserve the user's location.

problem: Sensor-like shaders overlap photography but use different simulated geometry.
preserve: Shader transfer functions and hidden-surface representation.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 2 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 18 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_03__sensor-and-technical-shaders.md.
validation: Compare identical geometry in sensor-capture and CGI-shader representations.

problem: Comic language sometimes imports page structure, heroes or franchise-era content.
preserve: Inking, shadow mass, halftone and contour hierarchy.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 14 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 3 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 6 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__comic-book-styles.md.
validation: A single requested image must not grow panels or speech balloons automatically.

problem: Child-oriented rendering mixes body-proportion changes with watercolor and cut-paper media.
preserve: Accessible silhouettes, shape simplification and medium handling.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 14 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 3 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 6 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__children-s-illustration.md.
validation: A character's proportions remain stable unless the selected profile explicitly changes them.

problem: Print techniques and named design traditions share mandatory poster/layout conventions.
preserve: Graphic hierarchy, ink layers and surface reproduction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 17 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__editorial-and-poster.md.
validation: An image treatment does not invent slogans, frames or a poster layout.

problem: Speedpainting shares a category with sheets, iterations, environments and product concepts.
preserve: Economical value studies and readable design exploration.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 29 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 29; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__concept-art.md.
validation: The selected deliverable controls layout; a paint method alone does not.

problem: Related print techniques recur elsewhere and share broad quality boilerplate.
preserve: Differences in cut, bite, pressure, hatching and negative space.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 5 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__ink-and-print.md.
validation: The same neutral subject should reveal identifiable differences between linocut, etching and scratchboard.

problem: Blueprints, HUDs and anatomy sheets require structural conventions, not generic free composition.
preserve: Views, callout hierarchy and diagram readability.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 6 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 14 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_04__technical-and-reference-sheets.md.
validation: A reference sheet remains a sheet; no placeholder gibberish is presented as valid technical data.

problem: The former DNA steered many styles toward school, assassin and battle scenes; the active fields now describe transferable drawing mechanics.
preserve: Contour energy, value blocks and motion emphasis.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 40 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 27 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 40; details in overhaul/audits/pack_05__modern-shonen-action.md.
validation: An ordinary quiet activity keeps its action and location under the drawing style.

problem: The former DNA mixed robots, hangars and battles with mechanical linework; the active fields now describe transferable rendering instead.
preserve: Mechanical line precision, hard shadows and color separation.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 30 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 3 card briefs per preset for all 30; details in overhaul/audits/pack_05__mecha-cyberpunk.md.
validation: A requested plant remains a plant rather than becoming a robot or hangar scene.

problem: The former DNA steered named journeys, cooking and fantasy worlds toward fixed scenes; the active fields now describe transferable painted and cel mechanics.
preserve: Painted atmosphere, cel softness and material stylization.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 30 fantasy-anime finishes rewritten with concrete line, shadow, background and finish mechanisms and pulled apart where they overlapped; 27 anime-title names renamed to their look (old names kept as search aliases); a neutral household task stays that task; 90 new briefs with original adult characters.
validation: A neutral household task must not become a fantasy quest or cooking vignette.

problem: Dark narrative descriptors, violence and world identity share repeated visual templates.
preserve: Value compression, sharpness hierarchy and controlled unease.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 30 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 1 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 30; details in overhaul/audits/pack_05__dark-fantasy-seinen.md.
validation: A gentle prompt remains gentle in content while its visual treatment changes.

problem: These entries intentionally guide motion and staging; the former shared router forced danger, opponents and stock action scenes.
preserve: Directional energy and clear action hierarchy.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 5 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 15 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_05__action-motion-setpieces.md.
validation: Use a requested action and verify that its staging improves without inventing opponents, sports gear, extra props or danger.

problem: Different pigments are expanded with interchangeable quality language.
preserve: Brush load, edge transitions, opacity and layering.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 15 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 5 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__traditional-painting.md.
validation: Changing medium alters edges and layering while subject and framing remain constant.

problem: Tool names can be diluted by shared sketch/quality prose.
preserve: Pressure, line continuity, erasure, smudge and paper response.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 15 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 4 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 5 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__drawing-sketching.md.
validation: Graphite, charcoal and pen remain distinguishable on the same simple object.

problem: Print families recur in packs_04,10,11,17 with overlapping naming.
preserve: Ink transfer, plate marks, registration and substrate behavior.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 15 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 4 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 5 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__printmaking.md.
validation: Blind comparisons must distinguish the process without requiring a particular scene.

problem: Digital painting and vector looks are mixed with concept outputs and low-poly construction.
preserve: Edge economy, fill logic and digital mark handling.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 15 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 5 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 5 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__digital-art.md.
validation: A digital painting preset must not force a concept board or 3D object render.

problem: Embroidery, assemblage and photo overlays mix surface treatment with object construction.
preserve: Layer order, adhesion, stitch and substrate interaction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__mixed-media.md.
validation: A stitched image effect must not silently replace a person's clothing or anatomy.

problem: Hardware references mix palette/cluster limits with camera effects such as Mode 7.
preserve: Pixel clusters, palette allocation, dithering and deliberate resolution.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 15 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__retro-game-visual-systems.md.
validation: A fixed-camera subject demonstrates cluster differences; perspective changes require the profile.

problem: Game rendering, tile representation, parallax and HUD design compete in one group.
preserve: Readability at game scale and coherent interface/asset construction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 20 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 2 renamed (old names kept as search aliases); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_06__game-art-directions-ui.md.
validation: A sprite stays an asset unless gameplay or interface layout is explicitly requested.

problem: Interior directions specify furnishing and construction, not a universally portable image style.
preserve: Spatial material palettes and furniture/construction vocabulary.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 16 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 4 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__interior-design-systems.md.
validation: Preserve requested room function and constraints; do not add the sample furniture bundle.

problem: Architectural identities imply structural changes that conflict with strict reference preservation.
preserve: Massing, facade rhythm and construction logic.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 13 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 7 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__architectural-movements-and-vernaculars.md.
validation: A preserve-mode photo is not structurally rebuilt; reinterpretation can apply requested design changes.

problem: Transit, conservatory and library concepts force a place through euphemistic names.
preserve: Patina, circulation and domain-specific spatial organization.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 9 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 11 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__civic-infrastructure-and-specialty-spaces.md.
validation: A requested room must not become a station or library under a surface treatment.

problem: Garden styles prescribe site organization and plant groupings.
preserve: Ground-plane rhythm, planting density and path hierarchy.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 10 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 10 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__landscape-and-garden-systems.md.
validation: Do not introduce a garden where no landscape transformation was requested.

problem: Fantasy architectural names still encode forge, sanctuary or fortress subjects.
preserve: Scale relationships, silhouettes and construction motifs.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 13 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 7 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__fantasy-and-mythic-architecture.md.
validation: A neutral structure keeps its function without receiving a fixed fantasy landmark.

problem: Miniature media are tied to architecture and toy systems.
preserve: Seams, paper thickness, scale cues and handmade construction.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 10 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 10 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__toy-craft-and-miniature-architecture.md.
validation: A requested object can use miniature construction without turning into a building.

problem: Pod, orbital and cloud worlds are mixed with genuine spatial paradoxes.
preserve: Repetition, circulation and deliberate geometric discontinuity.
proposedAction: Overhaul v2: 9 presets rewritten with concrete mechanisms; 11 new presets (pending cards); 3 card briefs per preset for all 20; details in overhaul/audits/pack_07__megastructure-and-impossible-space.md.
validation: Requested geometry remains stable in preserve mode; a paradox profile advertises structural change.

problem: Fashion silhouettes are presented alongside general image styles.
preserve: Cut, proportion, garment construction and fabric behavior.
proposedAction: Retain as wardrobe directions requiring deliberate clothing changes. Overhaul: DNA rewritten per garment system (fit, fabric, palette, fashion light) and 11 new wardrobe directions added to reach 20.
validation: A preserved outfit is unchanged; a wardrobe request changes clothing, not identity or location.

problem: Subcultural names bundle attire, lifestyle props and scenery.
preserve: Garment layering, utility and material combinations.
proposedAction: Focus wardrobe rules; leave venue, props and social narrative to the user. Overhaul: DNA rewritten per subculture garment code and 5 new directions (emo scene, visual kei, mod, decora, metal battle vest) added to reach 20.
validation: Changing attire does not automatically add a festival, vehicle or street scene.

problem: Historical costume entries can replace both the outfit and the surrounding era.
preserve: Garment structure and recognizable construction references.
proposedAction: Keep provenance specific; separate wardrobe transformation from historical environment. Overhaul: DNA rewritten as period garment systems that leave the setting to the prompt, and 9 new period wardrobes (Byzantine, Heian, Regency, Ottoman, medieval working dress, 1940s utility, Belle Epoque, Tang, Mughal) added to reach 20.
validation: A modern setting stays modern when only the costume is requested.

problem: Space, fantasy and craft clothing directions can dictate character roles.
preserve: Fastening, silhouette, protective layers and constructed detail.
proposedAction: Transfer distinct garment construction and material behavior while preserving the requested wearer, role and setting. Overhaul: three briefs per preset on varied wearers and settings to test identity retention, plus Chitin Insectoid Armor to reach 20.
validation: A new outfit preserves identity, pose and requested role.

problem: Fabric modifiers share a group with full-body material transformations such as stone.
preserve: Weave, drape, gloss and surface response.
proposedAction: Split local textile treatment from whole-object material replacement; require explicit targets. Overhaul: every preset now declares its target (garments only, or whole figure) in subject_treatment, DNA rewritten per material behavior, and three briefs per preset.
validation: Only the selected garment or object changes material.

problem: Material properties retain literal samples and habitat cues in rendering text.
preserve: Grain, pores, scale, reflectance and surface irregularity.
proposedAction: Keep material identity, remove sample-object/setting language and require an explicit target. Overhaul: DNA rewritten per material behavior with an explicit target rule and no habitat cues; three briefs per preset apply the material to unexpected targets.
validation: Raw oak applies to the requested object, not a mandatory plank at a lumber yard.

problem: Wall, tire and panel nouns mix source objects with finish behavior.
preserve: Manufacturing marks, seams, roughness and directional finish.
proposedAction: Separate material from source product; retain assembly profiles for structures like chain link. Overhaul: DNA describes the finish, not the source object, with explicit targets; three briefs per preset.
validation: Brushed metal treatment does not replace the target with its source product.

problem: Weathering templates bundle corrosion, collapse and abandonment beyond surface finish.
preserve: Local wear, deposition, staining and age gradients.
proposedAction: Make damage intensity and target explicit; keep structural collapse out of mild surface modifiers. Overhaul: every preset is a surface-level treatment with default moderate intensity and intact structure, plus 7 new weathering modes (salt crust, sun fade, soot, woodworm, acid etch, lichen, ash fall) to reach 20.
validation: A lightly weathered object does not become a ruin or change silhouette.

problem: Textiles, frost and chalk share compress/fuzz/smear boilerplate despite different mechanics.
preserve: Fibers, dry particle response and frost behavior.
proposedAction: Author each mechanism separately; avoid applying every tactile verb to every surface. Overhaul: each preset names one hand-feel mechanism, plus 12 new tactile surfaces to reach 20.
validation: Felt remains fibrous, chalk remains particulate and frost remains crystalline.

problem: Emission, fluid, particles and confetti can add an entire event or environment.
preserve: Boundary behavior, motion direction and local light contribution.
proposedAction: Require a target and contain the effect; separate surface behavior from emitted particles. Overhaul: every effect is contained on or around the named target with no new event, plus 8 new contained effects to reach 20.
validation: A subtle effect does not engulf the whole image or add unrelated props.

problem: Distinct visual systems share a generic flatten/tessellate/rotate template.
preserve: Plane relationships, repetition and hierarchy of geometric units.
proposedAction: Rewrite around each system's actual construction; retain provenance and explicit distortion boundaries. Overhaul: DNA rewritten per construction system, Mondrian renamed De Stijl Grid, and 10 new geometric systems added to reach 20.
validation: Compare identical content; preserve silhouette unless a structural transform is selected.

problem: Alcohol ink, smoke and liquid imagery mix surface media with literal fluid subjects.
preserve: Flow boundaries, pooling, diffusion and layering.
proposedAction: Separate fluid image-making from adding smoke or liquid objects to a scene. Overhaul: every preset makes the image through its fluid process and never adds liquid props, plus 10 new fluid processes to reach 20.
validation: A fluid illustration remains about the requested subject.

problem: Glitch, CRT, ASCII and halftone use different representation units but share noise language.
preserve: Block displacement, scan structure, glyph density and dot placement.
proposedAction: Split signal effects from glyph/print representation; avoid generic blanket noise. Overhaul: each preset declares whether it is a signal failure or a representation unit and applies one unit at controlled strength, plus 10 new artifacts to reach 20.
validation: Effects remain distinguishable and do not obscure the requested content by default.

problem: Dream moods, world genres and perspective distortions are pooled together.
preserve: Unexpected formal relationships and controlled ambiguity.
proposedAction: Separate mood, theme and structural distortion; do not force familiar liminal props or places. Overhaul: each preset declares distortion, mood or theme, artist-named presets renamed to techniques, and 5 new dream mechanisms added to reach 20.
validation: Strangeness emerges from form, not a mandatory corridor or empty pool.

problem: Textile motifs mix surface tiling with garment and embroidery construction.
preserve: Repeat, motif scale, orientation and border behavior.
proposedAction: Treat motif as a surface modifier; make support/output and structural stitches explicit. Overhaul: every motif applies to a named target surface and states whether it is printed, woven, dyed, knitted or stitched; 7 new patterns added to reach 20.
validation: A pattern follows the requested surface without becoming a wallpaper sample.

problem: Wood, carbon, rust and other surfaces overlap the material catalogue.
preserve: Coherent material response and macro-to-micro scale.
proposedAction: Compare with pack_09; keep distinct artistic simplifications, group mere palette variants. Overhaul: pack_10 surfaces are decorative surface patterns (figure, veining, motif) distinct from pack_09 physical materials; 9 new decorative finishes added to reach 20.
validation: Same target and lighting reveal whether the variant is materially different.

problem: Blueprint, QR and circuit looks imply valid technical or machine-readable information.
preserve: Line hierarchy, routing and modular information structure.
proposedAction: Label stylized diagrams as illustrative; do not claim generated QR or measurements are functional. Overhaul: every diagram preset is illustrative with unreadable marks and no working codes or real data; 15 new diagram languages added to reach 20.
validation: Generated decoration is not described as a verified code, circuit or measured plan.

problem: Pointillism, mosaic and stained glass share a template despite different units and joins.
preserve: Dot mixing, tesserae boundaries and leaded-cell structure.
proposedAction: Keep separate unit construction and light behavior, not just different names. Overhaul: each preset names its unit, joint and light behavior; Seurat preset renamed Pointillism; 17 new unit systems added to reach 20.
validation: The same image uses clearly different units without becoming a window or tile sample.

problem: Neon tubes, foil and letterpress combine emissive and physical print effects.
preserve: Glow confinement, metallic transfer and shallow impression.
proposedAction: Separate emissive modifier from foil and pressure processes; preserve optional output context. Overhaul: each preset is labeled emissive modifier or physical print process with its own light or support rules; 17 new finishes (7 emissive, 10 print) added to reach 20.
validation: A foil finish must not invent an invitation or mandatory signage.

problem: Toy brands, construction media and collectible proportions are bundled.
preserve: Joints, seams, material scale and handmade irregularity.
proposedAction: Extract craft rendering; keep collectible-body changes as a representation profile. Overhaul: each preset is one construction method, brand names replaced with generic ones (Lego, Funko, Play-Doh), collectible proportion change declared explicitly; 2 new crafts added to reach 20.
validation: A craft image does not become a fixed toy silhouette unless requested.

problem: Chalkboard, tattoo, stained glass and broadcast craft are grouped as a miscellaneous remainder.
preserve: Support-specific marks and image hierarchy.
proposedAction: Rehome by medium; keep tattoo flash layout separate from ink treatment. Overhaul: each preset is one physical making technique, tattoo flash keeps its sheet layout, three vague names made concrete, and 13 mediums checked against the catalog (pyrography, scrimshaw, gyotaku, folded papercut, rosemaling, black lacquer miniature, ink blot, pressed flowers, hooked rug, glass engraving, punched tin, pastiglia, oil on copper).
validation: An ink treatment does not become a tattoo sheet or broadcast puppet scene.

problem: Emoji, pixel constraints and world aesthetics have incompatible scopes.
preserve: Palette, clustering and coherent digital finish.
proposedAction: Split representation limits from thematic directions; remove generic catch-all placement. Overhaul: each aesthetic names the concrete signals that make it recognizable, grimdark drops franchise armor, vague names made concrete (vaporwave mall, psychedelic recursion), and 3 new aesthetics added (goblincore, dungeon synth cassette art, southern gothic).
validation: A pixel style must not inject a futuristic world or emoji facial features.

problem: Platter, candy world and commercial lighting mix subject recipes and portable treatments.
preserve: Food-light response and editorial surface detail.
proposedAction: Keep recipes that intentionally specify food; extract illumination and illustration separately. Overhaul: food stays the subject (named dishes are shot with the treatment, other subjects are built or plated as food), brand names replaced (Michelin, Candy Land), and 9 new food looks added (medieval feast, night market, retro aspic, preserves, charcuterie, molecular, open fire, pulled sugar, ramen).
validation: The food recipe can remain literal; its lighting derivative must work on non-food content.

problem: Scale, sensor style and literal specimen content are conflated.
preserve: Depth cues, detail scale and sensor-specific appearance.
proposedAction: Separate magnification profile from specimen subject and illustrative cellular themes. Overhaul: each preset is one magnification method plus the texture it reveals, prompt subjects are shown at that scale or emerge from the texture, brand name replaced (Velcro), duplicate name made specific (Carbon Fiber Weave Macro); no new presets needed (24).
validation: Do not invent scientific observations or replace an object with an insect eye.

problem: Two technical entries overlap both sensor capture and CGI shader groups.
preserve: Different sensor-style representations.
proposedAction: Compare exact mechanics across packs and cross-link rather than cloning future additions. Overhaul: each preset is one real instrument output that keeps subject geometry; the two generic entries became distinct instruments (dual-energy baggage X-ray, white-hot thermal imager), and 18 new instruments were checked against existing sensor presets (neutron, terahertz, event camera, spectrogram, reflectography, palimpsest, acoustic camera, tractography, EBSD, AFM, fluoroscopy, water vapor, mass spec, streak, capsule endoscopy, radio telescope, H-alpha, all-sky).
validation: Keep illustrative x-ray separate from actual diagnostic interpretation.

problem: A single blueprint entry duplicates navigation, not necessarily identical behavior.
preserve: Blueprint linework and output conventions.
proposedAction: Place it with technical representations; compare against existing blueprint presets before merging. Overhaul: the third catalog blueprint became a distinct used workshop blueprint; 19 new drafting conventions checked against blueprint, patent, cutaway, exploded, section, isometric, wiring and knotwork presets (hachure map, lines plan, piping iso, star fort, escapement, invention notebook, axonometric, figure-ground, lighting plot, crease pattern, knot steps, dance steps, weaving draft, survey plat, gear train, rigging, elevation, garden plan, stereotomy).
validation: A structural drawing remains explicitly illustrative, without invented measurement accuracy.

problem: Named game captures require routes, enemies, rooms and HUD cues, despite transferable wording.
preserve: Game-scale pixel/render readability and camera conventions.
proposedAction: Keep specialized capture profiles; derive visual-only styles without mandatory urban combat staging.
validation: A derivative respects arbitrary content; original profile is clearly labeled gameplay capture.

problem: Library, pilgrimage and temple setpieces remain embedded in the visual fields.
preserve: Capture finish, depth organization and playable silhouettes.
proposedAction: Separate game's visual representation from its sample encounter and location.
validation: An unrelated subject is not turned into a boss room or pilgrimage scene.

problem: Carrier, freight and defense scenarios substitute missions for style.
preserve: Hard-surface material hierarchy and strategy/action camera logic.
proposedAction: Retain deliberate game camera profiles; move mission and landmark nouns to examples.
validation: The profile preserves game readability without requiring the named mission.

problem: Battle formations and siege narratives are built into category templates.
preserve: Unit scale, terrain readability and tactical framing.
proposedAction: Separate tactical representation from battle story and faction design.
validation: A peaceful tactical scene stays peaceful; a battle occurs only when requested.

problem: Racing, sport and tactical references prescribe unrelated activity types.
preserve: Motion readability and competitive-space framing.
proposedAction: Make activity/camera scope explicit and extract rendering-only derivatives.
validation: A racing camera is not silently applied to a portrait treatment.

problem: Hunt, forge, survival and extraction scenarios impose location and danger.
preserve: Terrain value grouping and game-engine atmosphere.
proposedAction: Keep capture profiles specialized; remove sample missions from portable derivatives.
validation: A quiet outdoor request must not acquire hunters, monsters or objectives.

problem: Stealth missions, traps and boss scenes mix story content with engine finish.
preserve: Occlusion, visibility hierarchy and controlled environmental contrast.
proposedAction: Separate encounter direction from graphics and camera profile.
validation: A requested object remains the subject instead of becoming a mandatory horror encounter.

problem: Puzzle rooms and adventure hubs dictate puzzle props or specific traversal spaces.
preserve: Spatial legibility, interaction scale and distinct render families.
proposedAction: Retain puzzle/layout recipes as profiles; extract material/palette treatment independently.
validation: No unrequested puzzle mechanism, HUD or game objective is added by a visual-only derivative.

problem: Foundational anime entries still use city, hangar and shrine story nouns.
preserve: Cel value grouping, edge hierarchy and restrained stylization.
proposedAction: Extract basic drawing and shading systems; keep source scene titles as search-only metadata. Overhaul: each preset now states one genre look (line, cel, palette, light) usable with any prompt, scenes moved into three briefs per preset, and 5 new genre looks added (sky pirates, cursed blade dark fantasy, monster tamer, beast rider, midnight mountain racing).
validation: A neutral object must not inherit the sample city or shrine.

category: 2. Slice Of Life, School And Music
problem: School, music and cafe contexts prescribe activities instead of just intimate visual treatment.
preserve: Small gestures, soft light and everyday-scale staging.
proposedAction: Separate slice-of-life mood from venues and roles. Overhaul: each preset is a light-and-mood look (palette, light, line) rather than a venue, venues only appear in the three briefs as tests, one vague backstage entry renamed, and 15 new mood looks added (concert spotlight, golden hour, winter breath, night lamp, 90s cel, garage band, recital, seaside haze, dawn mist, rooftop wind, late train, soft focus, club clutter, library sunbeam, choir light).
validation: A requested home activity stays at home without mandatory idol or cafe content.

problem: Studio-era and magical-character references blend visual grammar with iconic narrative markers.
preserve: Line elasticity, cel polish and expressive staging.
proposedAction: Document references separately and derive transferable rendering; transformations remain explicit profiles. Overhaul: DNA already carries portable line and cel mechanics, so this pass audits it unchanged and adds three original briefs per preset (40); franchise names stay as search identity while every brief uses original characters and places.
validation: No fixed costume, character or magical sequence is imported solely through a name.

problem: Shared warmth, school and hobby templates reduce distinctive styles to similar cozy scenes.
preserve: Microacting, proportion rhythm and soft edge control.
proposedAction: Transfer distinct line, shadow, texture and color mechanics without imposing activities or venues; compare neutral actions after rerendering. Overhaul: DNA already carries portable mechanics, so this pass keeps it and writes three original briefs per preset (30), each built to show that mechanic on an everyday moment.
validation: Different styles remain distinguishable without changing the activity to a hobby vignette.

problem: Many differently named entries repeat the same broad template and motion vocabulary.
preserve: Specific contour, shading and compositional decisions.
proposedAction: Keep the distinct drawing mechanics, with requested-content preservation and defect-specific negatives. Compare the regenerated cards and cross-subject images before grouping adjacent variants.
validation: Blind comparisons should reveal the rendering difference rather than the renamed scene.

problem: Era and source-title cues prescribe pioneers, heists and space drama.
preserve: Cel edge behavior, painted backdrops and restrained frame-era artifacts.
proposedAction: Keep the SP16-001 study and the distinct legacy cel treatments; compare rerendered subjects before grouping adjacent variants.
validation: A contemporary subject stays contemporary under a retro cel treatment.

problem: Character archetypes and iconic genres dominate despite renamed display labels.
preserve: Shadow group count, lineweight and color separation.
proposedAction: Keep contour echoes, cel-value grouping, line rhythm and material-aware highlights without mandatory characters or scenes. Remove bare text bans; compare regenerated subjects before grouping variants.
validation: Keep action, setting and identity constant across the comparison set.

problem: Romance, clan comedy and specific narrative beats are mixed with digital-era appearance.
preserve: Compositing softness, cel line handling and background integration.
proposedAction: Keep the documented line, timing, value and compositing mechanics without mandatory story beats. SP05-156 has no distinct technical mechanism in its source; leave its distinctness pending comparison instead of inventing one from the name.
validation: A neutral task must not become a romance or clan-comedy scene.

problem: Many auteur-like titles share long templates, masking their actual visual differences.
preserve: Specific layout, edge, color and background relationships.
proposedAction: Preserve distinct contour, value, timing and background mechanics without forcing source scenes; rerender neutral subjects and compare the resulting styles.
validation: The difference is observable without iconic scenes or remembered characters.

problem: Sport, competition and team narratives are mandatory in many entries.
preserve: Anatomical gesture, speed cues and performance readability.
proposedAction: Separate motion/action profiles from drawing finish; retain sport-specific staging explicitly.
validation: A quiet gesture can use the drawing style without becoming a team competition.

problem: Medieval and samurai content is coupled to motion and solemn framing.
preserve: Gesture timing, line economy and group-value design.
proposedAction: Keep wardrobe/world direction separate from rendering and action profiles.
validation: A portrait keeps its outfit unless a costume transformation is deliberately selected.

problem: Horror samples prescribe institutions, puppets or cosmic events.
preserve: Negative-space tension, contour control and restrained contrast.
proposedAction: Extract visual unease without requiring a location, monster or violent story beat.
validation: A harmless subject remains harmless in content while visual tension changes.

problem: Ashen and gothic entries retain funerary/medieval nouns after display-name changes.
preserve: Heavy value planes, matte finish and controlled edge loss.
proposedAction: SP17-073 derives value-plane and edge treatment from SP17-001 while retaining the original ceremonial direction; compare with atlas CR-04 before promotion.
validation: An everyday object keeps its function and setting without becoming a relic.

problem: Print media are tied to dungeon, necromancy and monster-manual content.
preserve: Registration, spot inks, photocopy breakup and paper contrast.
proposedAction: Separate print grammar from dark-fantasy theme; group palette-only variants after testing.
validation: The print treatment works on non-fantasy content without adding monsters or page decoration.

problem: Tarot, bestiary and icon layouts are mixed with reusable ink techniques.
preserve: Contour hierarchy, solid blacks and sparse line detail.
proposedAction: Separate plate/card output profiles from mark-making; keep explicit format recipes available.
validation: Ink style alone does not add card borders, labels or a fixed creature crop.

problem: Armor, citadels and warfronts prescribe design and world content.
preserve: Material contrast, layered construction and controlled emissive details.
proposedAction: Keep design/world directions explicit; derive surface/render treatments without structures or gear.
validation: A render treatment does not add armor, machinery or an apocalyptic setting.

problem: Isometric ARPG, 2.5D spaces and portrait output have deliberate but incompatible layout scopes.
preserve: Game readability, camera conventions and portrait massing.
proposedAction: Separate camera/output profiles from dark rendering; preserve selected profile behavior.
validation: A portrait is not made isometric, and a game profile does not force a dungeon landmark.

problem: Three new handmade zine processes need comparison with existing dungeon print treatments and with one another.
preserve: The requested subject and action remain intact while torn paper, stencil ink or stamping constructs the image.
proposedAction: Keep the three mark mechanisms distinct; do not make dungeon props or page furniture mandatory.
validation: Compare an ordinary animal, a working object and a human action; inspect complete cards and transfer before visual acceptance.

problem: Airbrush and drybrush need clear medium identity without defaulting to stock cover scenes or realistic key art.
preserve: Requested content, silhouette and framing; the painting process changes the rendering.
proposedAction: Keep airbrush and drybrush as distinct portable painting mechanisms. Root visual review strengthened dominant sprayed gradients after a representative airbrush card drifted into bristle-painted concept art. Fantasy events remain confined to card briefs.
validation: Apply both processes to the same non-fantasy subject and inspect whether their marks remain distinguishable at card size.

problem: Silverpoint, resist, chalk, Conté and colored pencil require separate visible marks rather than a shared nostalgic fantasy scene.
preserve: Identity, materials, pose and camera from the user request.
proposedAction: Retain each drawing process as an independent style and keep fantasy subjects in representative cards only.
validation: Compare the five on the same ordinary subject and inspect whether support, line and pigment behavior remain distinct.

problem: Ten ink structures now cover direct marks, lifted ink and controlled tonal methods; overlapping print processes and cross-subject transfer still need visual comparison.
preserve: Subject identity, requested pose, framing and scene content.
proposedAction: Keep direct ink processes distinct from plate transfer; compare all ten across subjects before promoting or consolidating.
validation: Test an object, ordinary action, interior, exterior and graphic composition with fixed requested content.

problem: Ten print treatments now cover plate, transfer, exposure and screen mechanisms; image quality and transfer across subjects remain unproven.
preserve: Subject identity, requested pose, framing and scene content.
proposedAction: Keep reproduction processes distinct from surface-only texture and inspect representative cards before promotion.
validation: Test an object, ordinary action, interior, exterior and graphic composition with fixed requested content.

problem: Ten support and pigment mechanisms now span dry, wet, additive and subtractive treatment; their cross-subject behavior still needs visual review.
preserve: Subject identity, requested pose, framing and scene content.
proposedAction: Keep the paper or pigment mechanism visible without transferring a stock subject or support texture onto depicted materials.
validation: Test an object, ordinary action, interior, exterior and graphic composition with fixed requested content.

problem: Medium cues can collapse into a generic painted object.
preserve: Distinct glaze, acrylic, wash and drawing mark behavior.
proposedAction: Keep the medium process active and let the request select the subject.
validation: Apply each process to the same contemporary bicycle without changing its parts.

problem: Epic labels can force heroic figures or fantasy backdrops.
preserve: Edge control, pigment-like volume and grouped painted values.
proposedAction: Express scale through paint handling rather than a required heroic scene.
validation: A quiet domestic plant still shows the chosen paint treatment.

problem: Dark media labels can add horror content that was never requested.
preserve: Thorn-like incision, soot wash and broken pigment surfaces.
proposedAction: Transfer unsettling mark behavior without adding violence or monsters.
validation: A plain streetlamp can carry the mark treatment without becoming a horror scene.

problem: Narrative names can become a fixed fairytale setting.
preserve: Gouache planes, cel edges and controlled volume simplification.
proposedAction: Keep animation and storybook rendering separate from story content.
validation: A modern tram retains its form under each rendering language.

problem: Creature-card origins can pull every subject toward a creature design.
preserve: Contour economy, readable silhouette and controlled proportions.
proposedAction: Apply form design to the supplied subject without inventing a new character.
validation: A chair remains a chair while its shape language changes.

problem: Game and collection provenance can be mistaken for a required franchise character or costume.
preserve: Line density, cel modeling, highlight rhythm and painted finish.
proposedAction: Retain technical differences while keeping game and collection provenance out of the portable visual rules.
validation: An original adult gardener stays identifiable across all eight treatments.

problem: Impact language can force combat where the request has none.
preserve: Brush pressure, screen tone and crisp black-white value structure.
proposedAction: Use action marks only for requested motion; preserve quiet subjects.
validation: A stationary train platform gains manga mark language without an invented fight.

problem: Mechanical drafting can turn unrelated subjects into robots or products.
preserve: Boundaries and contact shadows of existing parts, restrained facet shading and industrial airbrush transitions.
proposedAction: Separate diagram framing from portable surface and line treatment.
validation: A ceramic flowerpot keeps its material and function under the style.

problem: Superhero and comic references can import a cast or panel story.
preserve: Contour weight, flat color, modeled ink and expressive simplification.
proposedAction: Make drawing grammar transferable without obligatory panels or heroes.
validation: A city bicycle can use the ink and color system without a costume.

problem: Print variants can collapse into the same paper-distress overlay.
preserve: Different carved, engraved, overprinted and registration marks.
proposedAction: Keep each reproduction process visibly distinct at card scale.
validation: The same bird silhouette shows a different mark construction in each process.

problem: Ornamental references can force a card border or literal symbol.
preserve: Leaded segments, geometric planes and flowing interior ornament.
proposedAction: Apply image-wide ornament styles to existing forms; keep filigree, gilding, porcelain and enamel effects local and frames optional.
validation: A plain lamp shows the color-cell or line treatment without a border.

problem: Craft sources can replace the requested object with a toy or unrelated diorama.
preserve: Clay, thread and paper construction cues with physical depth.
proposedAction: Apply the selected crafted rendering language while retaining the requested object's identity and real materials.
validation: A requested bicycle remains a bicycle when rendered as cut paper or clay.

problem: Historical card references can force obsolete labels, frames or nostalgia props.
preserve: Lithographic overlap, airbrush transitions and wax-pencil direction.
proposedAction: Use print-era techniques independently of collectible layout.
validation: A modern houseplant carries the medium without a caption or trading-card frame.

problem: Emblematic composition can turn every subject into a logo.
preserve: Flat color, positive-negative balance and line hierarchy.
proposedAction: Retain graphic economy while respecting the requested object and framing.
validation: A dog portrait stays a portrait, not a badge, under the style.

problem: Digital method names can become a generic retro or glossy filter.
preserve: Pixel clustering, selective dithering and measured polygon planes.
proposedAction: Keep each sampling or polygon style distinct; confine glass and displacement modifiers to their requested targets.
validation: The same street scene exposes distinct pixel, dither and facet methods.

problem: Medieval labels can add parchment, page frames and religious motifs by default.
preserve: Opaque pigment planes, value bands, interlace and controlled manuscript line.
proposedAction: Transfer the five image styles without an automatic codex page; use Scriptorium Page layout only when its structure profile is selected.
validation: A contemporary radio keeps its identity under the image styles; the page profile adds structure only when selected.

problem: Relief and intaglio methods can be flattened into one antique-paper texture.
preserve: Blockcut mass, burin weave and etched line direction.
proposedAction: Keep each physical print style distinct from aged-paper decoration; apply relief and intaglio modifiers only to requested accents over an existing base.
validation: The same leaf displays different relief and incision marks; disabling an accent modifier leaves the selected base intact.

problem: Textile, fresco, enamel and stained-glass references can import liturgical objects or architecture.
preserve: Woven planes, wool outlines, mineral pigment, enamel cells and leaded-light structure.
proposedAction: Apply the selected rendering technique to the requested form without importing its source object, building or use.
validation: A modern coat keeps its cut under each material study; switching techniques changes the marks, not the garment's use.

problem: Regional names risk becoming a generic exotic ornament.
preserve: Specific color-cell, spatial and geometric drawing structures.
proposedAction: Keep provenance visible in metadata and active rules technically precise.
validation: An ordinary animal retains its identity while each tradition differs in mark and space for reasons supported by its recorded source corpus.

problem: Revival illustration can be conflated with its medieval sources.
preserve: Dense shape masses, reserved light, ornamental line within existing forms and illustrated wash as distinct treatments.
proposedAction: Name the revival period accurately and avoid automatic fairytale scenes.
validation: A current-day garden tool shows revival drawing without a costume or story.

problem: Game references blend portrait, sprite, environment, HUD and camera obligations.
preserve: Era-specific raster, gouache and interface craft.
proposedAction: Keep content and camera guardrails explicit within each style, and transfer its rendering without inventing HUD or dungeon-map output.
validation: A requested portrait does not become a HUD or dungeon map unless selected.

problem: Retro pixels can degrade into a uniform mosaic filter.
preserve: Intentional palette limits, cluster shape and selective dither.
proposedAction: Keep cluster construction distinct per preset and avoid noisy upscaling.
validation: The same bird keeps its silhouette under all four distinct raster rules.

problem: Retro 3D can force a game camera or first-person composition.
preserve: Facet shading, angular planes and painted low-resolution texture.
proposedAction: Transfer geometry and texture treatment independently of viewpoint.
validation: A tabletop radio preserves the requested camera and gains low-poly treatment.

problem: RPG origins can require a combat grid or heroic party.
preserve: Transparent wash, opaque gouache, layered planes and compact pixel clusters.
proposedAction: Transfer each paint or pixel construction method while leaving game layout optional.
validation: The same quiet bicycle retains its viewpoint and parts under both painted and pixel treatments, without a tactical grid.

problem: Tabletop art, editorial layout and reproduction wear can be conflated.
preserve: Ink mass, painted shape and selective print wear.
proposedAction: Apply image styles without adding captions, card layout or statistics, which are not profiles in this category.
validation: A plain original creature portrait carries the style without a game card frame.

problem: Reference-sheet and raster techniques can add fabricated labels or forced props.
preserve: Flat planes, data-bounded diagrams and tactile raster modeling.
proposedAction: Keep the five image styles on the requested content and composition; only the selected Data-Bounded Reference Sheet profile may impose a sheet layout, and its facts must be supplied.
validation: A simple shoe diagram uses only legible supplied facts and no filler measurements.

problem: Combining media can erase the dominant technique, while a local pigment modifier can spread without a requested material target.
preserve: A primary medium with one controlled secondary accent.
proposedAction: State which process leads in each image style; apply the pigment modifier only to a named compatible target over its base.
validation: A single bird keeps form under the five image styles; toggling the pigment modifier changes only the selected material accent.

proposedAction: Apply reviewed characteristic motifs and construction to unspecified design choices; retain history and archive retired identities.
validation: A matched blue bicycle and modern-person pilot retained both subjects and made one narrow meander or incised motif legible; the refreshed composition was reviewed. Further subjects and user acceptance remain pending.
